name: West Midlands
description: West Midlands is a metropolitan county centred on Birmingham, Britain's second-largest city. It is a major economic and transport hub with a strong manufacturing heritage, a diverse population and a dense network of surrounding towns and cities.

places.name: Solihull
places.description: An affluent town in the West Midlands known for its Touchwood shopping centre and the Land Rover factory that has anchored its economy for decades.

places.name: Birmingham
places.description: England's second-largest city, built on centuries of metalworking and manufacturing, with an extensive canal network and a fast-growing modern skyline.

places.name: Coventry
places.description: A West Midlands city rebuilt after WWII bombing destroyed its medieval cathedral, whose ruins stand beside the striking modern cathedral built alongside them.

places.name: Dudley
places.description: A district in the Black Country, West Midlands, historically central to England's iron and coal industries, with Dudley Castle and Zoo standing above the town.

places.name: Sandwell
places.description: A district in the Black Country, West Midlands, formed from towns including West Bromwich and Oldbury, shaped by heavy industry and metalworking heritage.

places.name: Walsall
places.description: A town in the Black Country historically known as the centre of England's leather goods and saddlery trade, still reflected in its 'Saddlers' football club nickname.

places.name: Wolverhampton
places.description: A city in the West Midlands historically built on lock-making and heavy engineering, home to a striking medieval church and a strong football tradition.
